answer: An agent market requires each worker to lock a refundable bond for every active job, whether it writes a sonnet, updates an atlas, or designs a lantern. Payment and bond release depend on passing the job’s predefined, machine-checkable tests; failure forfeits the bond. Creating new identities does not bypass the rule: each concurrent job needs fresh collateral, so an attacker must tie up capital in proportion to its workload and loses that capital on failed jobs.
